slides.heading: Design Airbnb
slides.subtitle: SystemsExpert design walkthrough
slides.narration: In this lecture we design Airbnb. We'll follow the interview framework: clarify, set requirements, estimate, sketch the architecture, define the data and API, then dive into the hard parts and the trade-offs.

slides.heading: Clarifying questions
bullets: Search + booking + host listing management in scope? Payments?
Can two guests book overlapping dates? (No)
Scale of listings?
slides.narration: Start by clarifying the scope with your interviewer. Good questions here are: Search plus booking plus host listing management in scope? Payments? Can two guests book overlapping dates? (No). Scale of listings?

slides.heading: Functional requirements
bullets: Hosts create listings with availability
Guests search by location/dates/price
Guests book; double booking impossible
slides.narration: The functional requirements. Hosts create listings with availability. Guests search by location or dates or price. Guests book; double booking impossible.

slides.heading: Non-functional requirements
bullets: Search fast (< 300 ms)
Booking strongly consistent
slides.narration: The non-functional requirements. Search fast ( under 300 ms). Booking strongly consistent.

slides.heading: Capacity estimates
bullets: ~10M listings, ~100M searches/day (~1.2k/s), ~1M bookings/day
slides.narration: Now some rough capacity estimates, which drive the design. about 10M listings, about 100M searches per day (about 1.2k per s), about 1M bookings per day.

slides.heading: High-level architecture
slides.narration: Here's the high-level architecture. Guest connects to API. Host connects to API. API connects to Listings DB and Search index - geo plus filters and Bookings / availability DB and Payments. Listings DB connects to Change data capture. Change data capture connects to Search index - geo plus filters.

slides.heading: Data model
bullets: listings(id, host_id, geo, price, attributes)
availability(listing_id, date, status) PK(listing_id, date)
bookings(id, listing_id, guest_id, start, end, status)
slides.narration: Here is the data model. listings(id, host id, geo, price, attributes). availability(listing id, date, status) PK(listing id, date). bookings(id, listing id, guest id, start, end, status).

slides.heading: API
slides.narration: The API. The main endpoints are: GET search with lat and lng and radius and checkIn and checkOut and guests and priceMax; GET listings by id; POST listings; POST bookings. Each one is small, resource-oriented and easy to version.

slides.heading: No double booking
bullets: In one transaction, lock the availability rows for the date range (SELECT … FOR UPDATE) and mark them reserved; or insert into a table with a unique (listing_id, date) constraint.
Temporary holds expire if payment fails.
slides.narration: Deep dive: No double booking. In one transaction, lock the availability rows for the date range (SELECT FOR UPDATE) and mark them reserved; or insert into a table with a unique (listing id, date) constraint. Temporary holds expire if payment fails.

slides.heading: Search
bullets: Geo index (geohash/quadtree) in Elasticsearch with date availability filters; results may be slightly stale, so booking re-validates.
slides.narration: Deep dive: Search. Geo index (geohash or quadtree) in Elasticsearch with date availability filters; results may be slightly stale, so booking re-validates.

slides.heading: Payments
bullets: Authorise at booking, capture after check-in.
slides.narration: Deep dive: Payments. Authorise at booking, capture after check-in.

slides.heading: Trade-offs & alternatives
bullets: Search eventual consistency vs booking strong consistency
Per-date rows are simple; range types/interval trees are more compact
slides.narration: Finally, the key trade-offs. Search eventual consistency versus booking strong consistency. Per-date rows are simple; range types or interval trees are more compact.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Clarify scope, then functional + non-functional needs
Estimate load to size storage and fan-out
Core pieces: Guest, API, Host, Listings DB, Change data capture
Know your trade-offs and failure modes
slides.narration: To recap Airbnb: we clarified the scope, set functional and non-functional requirements, estimated the load, sketched an architecture built around Guest, API, Host, Listings DB, and walked through the deep dives and trade-offs. Practise explaining each decision out loud.
